pois.name: Queensland Museum
pois.intro: The Queensland Museum is the state museum of Queensland, funded by the Queensland Government, of natural history, cultural heritage, science and human achievement.

pois.name: Gallery of Modern Art
pois.intro: The Gallery of Modern Art is an art museum located within the Queensland Cultural Centre in the South Bank precinct of Brisbane, Queensland, Australia. The gallery is part of QAGOMA. Opened on 2 December 2006, the GOMA is Australia's largest gallery of modern and contemporary art.

pois.name: Brisbane City Botanic Gardens
pois.intro: The City Botanic Gardens is a heritage-listed botanic garden on Alice Street in Brisbane, Queensland, Australia. It was also known as Queen's Park.

pois.name: Lone Pine Koala Sanctuary
pois.intro: Lone Pine Koala Sanctuary is an 18-hectare koala sanctuary in the Brisbane suburb of Fig Tree Pocket in Queensland, Australia. Founded in 1927, it is the oldest and largest koala sanctuary of its kind in the world.

pois.name: Queensland Art Gallery
pois.intro: The Queensland Art Gallery is an art museum located in South Bank, Brisbane, Queensland, Australia. The gallery is part of QAGOMA. It complements the Gallery of Modern Art building, situated only 150 metres away.

pois.name: South Bank Parklands
pois.intro: The South Bank Parklands are located at South Bank within the suburb of South Brisbane in Brisbane, Queensland, Australia. The parkland, on the transformed site of Brisbane's World Expo 88, was officially opened to the public on 20 June 1992.

pois.name: Max Brenner Chocolate Bar
pois.intro: Max Brenner is an Israeli multinational chocolate restaurant and retail brand. The company operates 36 locations internationally, the majority of which are in Australia.

pois.name: HMAS Diamantina
pois.intro: HMAS Diamantina, named after the Diamantina River in Queensland, is a River-class frigate that served the Royal Australian Navy. Constructed in the mid-1940s, Diamantina was active from 1945 until 1946, was placed in reserve, then was recommissioned as a survey ship from 1959 until 1980.

pois.name: Mount Coot-tha Botanic Gardens
pois.intro: The Brisbane Botanic Gardens are located 7 kilometres from the Brisbane CBD at the foot of Brisbane's tallest mountain, Mount Coot-tha in the suburb of Mount Coot-tha, Queensland, Australia. The gardens receive around 1.4 million visitors a year.

pois.name: King George Square
pois.intro: King George Square is a public square located between Adelaide Street and Ann Street in Brisbane, Queensland, Australia. Brisbane City Hall is adjacent to the square.

pois.name: The Wheel of Brisbane
pois.intro: The Wheel of Brisbane is an observation wheel in Brisbane, Queensland, Australia. It is 60 metres tall.

pois.name: Whites Hill Reserve
pois.intro: Whites Hill is a hill in the suburb of Camp Hill, City of Brisbane, Queensland, Australia. Surrounding the hill is Whites Hill Reserve, a public reserve occupying the south of the suburbs of Camp Hill and Carina Heights.

pois.name: Museum of Lands, Mapping and Surveying
pois.intro: The Museum of Lands, Mapping and Surveying is a museum at 317 Edward Street, Brisbane, Queensland, Australia. It collects and exhibits material relating to the surveying of Queensland and the maps created.

pois.name: Commissariat Store
pois.intro: The Commissariat Store is a heritage-listed storehouse at 115–127 William Street, Brisbane City, City of Brisbane, Queensland, Australia. It is bordered by William Street, Queen's Wharf Road and the Brisbane River, and is the birthplace of Queensland.

pois.name: Chinatown
pois.description: Chinatown in the heart of Fortitude Valley
pois.intro: Chinatown, Brisbane is a cultural, retail and dining precinct in Fortitude Valley, Brisbane, Australia. It is centred on Chinatown Mall, a pedestrian area which occupies all of Duncan Street.

pois.name: Queensland Maritime Museum
pois.intro: The Queensland Maritime Museum is located on the southern bank of the Brisbane River just south of the South Bank Parklands and Queensland Cultural Centre precinct of Brisbane, and close to the Goodwill Bridge.

pois.name: Boggo Road Gaol
pois.intro: H.M. Prison Brisbane, commonly known as Boggo Road Gaol, was Queensland's main prison from the 1880s to the 1980s. By the time it closed, it had become notorious for poor conditions and rioting.

pois.name: Sir Thomas Brisbane Planetarium
pois.intro: The Sir Thomas Brisbane Planetarium is located on the grounds of the Brisbane Botanic Gardens in the suburb of Mount Coot-tha, Brisbane, Queensland, Australia.

pois.name: Old Museum
pois.intro: The Old Museum Building is a heritage-listed former exhibition building, former museum and now performance venue in Bowen Hills, Brisbane, Queensland, Australia. It is made from 1.3 million red bricks and bordered by Gregory Terrace and the Exhibition Grounds.

pois.name: New Farm Deli
pois.description: Deli, cafe, lots of great italian meat and cheese

pois.name: The Hideout Specialty Coffee on Adelaide
Brisbane Arcade
pois.description: The ‘Jewel in the Crown’ of Brisbane, Brisbane Arcade is Brisbane’s oldest shopping arcade. Believed to have been under construction in 1923 with the first store openings in 1924, the arcade’s history spans nearly a century.
pois.intro: Brisbane Arcade is a heritage-listed shopping arcade at 160 Queen Street through to Adelaide Street in the Brisbane CBD, City of Brisbane, Queensland, Australia. Designed by Richard Gailey Jr.

pois.name: Wintergarden
pois.intro: Wintergarden is a shopping centre in Brisbane, Queensland, Australia. It contains over 60 specialty stores over three levels.

pois.name: Macarthur Central
pois.intro: MacArthur Central, also known as MacArthur Central Shopping Centre, in Brisbane, Australia, is a four level shopping centre that incorporates an English Renaissance styled heritage-listed building known as MacArthur Chambers. MacArthur Central is on the north-east corners of Queen Street, Edward Street and Elizabeth Street.

pois.name: Victoria Park / Barrambin
pois.intro: Victoria Park, also known by its Turrbal name of Barrambin, is a heritage-listed park located in Spring Hill and Herston in Brisbane, Australia. It was added to the Queensland Heritage Register on 3 December 2007.

pois.name: Anzac Square
pois.intro: ANZAC Square is a heritage-listed town square and war memorial located between Ann Street and Adelaide Street, in Brisbane, Queensland, Australia. It is a state memorial to the men and women who participated in overseas armed service and is named in honour of the Australian and New Zealand Army Corps.

pois.name: New Farm Park
pois.intro: New Farm Park is a heritage-listed riverfront public park at 137 Sydney Street, New Farm, City of Brisbane, Queensland, Australia. It was designed by Albert Herbert Foster and built from 1914 to 1950 by Gladwin Legge & Co.

pois.name: Spring Hill Baths
pois.intro: Spring Hill Baths is a heritage-listed swimming pool at 14 Torrington Street, Spring Hill, City of Brisbane, Queensland, Australia. It was designed by Thomas Kirk and built from 1886 to 1913 by William M Park.

pois.name: Roma Street Parklands
pois.intro: Roma Street Parkland covers 11 hectares in the centre of the City of Brisbane, Queensland, Australia. The Roma Street Parkland is adjacent to the former Brisbane Transit Centre and the Roma Street railway station from which it takes its name.

pois.name: Musgrave Park
pois.intro: Musgrave Park is a park in South Brisbane, Queensland, Australia. The park is bordered by Edmonstone, Russell, and Cordelia Streets, and Brisbane State High School, and has an area of 63,225 square metres.

terminalResolution.notes: Added the Brisbane International Cruise Terminal (from OpenStreetMap), which takes most ships since 2020; Bretts Wharf is kept for smaller ships. The rest are river ferry terminals.
